summary: A row of headline numbers, each on its own card with an icon, its change against the period before and a sparkline. A period switch, such as 7 days, 30 days and Quarter, rolls every number and line to the new values at once. It works as the top row of an agent dashboard, for numbers like runs, hours saved and spend.
use: At the top of a dashboard, to show the few numbers people check first.
When you want to show an agent's runs, time saved or cost at a glance.
When the same numbers need comparing across a few fixed periods.
features: Each card shows an icon, a label, a large number that rolls to its value, and a change percentage, green from 0 and red below.
A sparkline per card draws in from the left, in the card's `color`, or the chart palette in order: the accent, then violet, green and orange.
Each stat has one entry in `values` per entry in `periods`, and switching the period updates every card together.
Hovering a card shows the period's `compare` text, like "vs previous 30 days".
`prefix` and `suffix` wrap the number, like "$" or "h".
`sparkRange` puts every sparkline on the same scale; by default each card scales to its own lowest and highest point.
The change against the previous period sits in a tinted chip: green with dark text when it rises, red when it falls.
Four across on a wide screen, and two by two on tablets and phones.
a11y: The period switch is a role="group" labelled "Period", with aria-pressed on the active option.
The sparkline draw-in is skipped, and number roll-ups finish at once, when the user prefers reduced motion.

faq.a: No. The large number is rounded to a whole number and written with thousands separators, like 1,730. Pass a smaller unit, or put the unit in `suffix`, if you need finer detail.

faq.q: How do I compare sparklines across cards?
faq.a: Pass `sparkRange` as [bottom, top]. Every card then uses the same scale, so a taller line means a bigger value on every card.

faq.q: How do I hide the period switch?
faq.a: Pass a single entry in `periods`, with one value per stat. The switch only shows with two or more periods.
